doc.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

title: Getting his first trumpet at nine and learning from his father
summary: Parents surrounded him with music and art; he got a trumpet at nine, shelved it, then secretly played from his father's books in high school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did your father and your mother encourage you to a life in the arts? Because I know you were thinking about being a visual artist also?

Right. Well they encouraged me in the way that they presented me the home that I grew up with with all of that. Because my father was a visual artist as well and my uncles were visual artists. So I had all that around me. I was seeing that, I was into music, seeing all the drawings and the paintings and stuff. So it was there. It was just like saying if you want it there it is. You make a choice, do I want to do this. I wasn’t forced. I got my first trumpet when I was nine. And in New Orleans with the shotgun house we had those high ceilings and the lights with the long string and wire with a light bulb hanging from the ceiling you know, and you would pull the string. We didn’t have the fixtures and the chandeliers and all that stuff. So my ninth birthday I woke up and dangling from the light was my first trumpet. So man it was a novelty for me. I had my trumpet and I was, you know. So after a few weeks it wore off. And I stuck it under the bed and when I went to high school I started playing again. I wasn’t forced to do it. My father was teaching me but I felt so dumb, that he was such a great musician and all that, I didn’t want to let him know how much I didn’t know which was crazy because, you know. But he was trying to teach me and I didn’t know — so much I didn’t know — but I was young and stuff. So what I did later on I would listen to him practice and playing and when he would leave I’d go and get his books and play what he was playing you know. So all of a sudden boom, here I was I was playing. And on my mother’s side of my family I had great musicians who played with Louis Armstrong. I had some — my mother’s maiden name
